summary: 11 concrete, comment-endorsed recommendations from 30 fully crawled Hacker News front-page stories.
telegram_footer: 11 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: Indigene
items.summary: A browser-based native-plant finder tailored to your exact location.
items.why_included: A commenter found its local recommendations useful and praised its explanatory diagrams.
items.evidence: A user in New England said the tool gave “great recs” for their land and another praised its plant-size diagrams.

evidence_sources.author: nja
evidence_sources.excerpt: Wow, this is a lovely tool, and it's clearly built with a lot of your own knowledge! I'm in New England and this has some great recs for my land. One slight piece of feedback: it's pretty clear a lot of the text was output of AI. IME (and just _my_ E, of course), this detracts somewhat from the authority of the page, as it makes it seem more like it just came from a conversation with Claude, rather than from your knowledge filtered through building an app. Might be worth doing a couple of passes to tighten up and human-ize it a bit :). (since it's open source, I suppose I could always PR myself if you'd be open to it)

evidence_sources.author: lelandbatey
evidence_sources.excerpt: You've done a great job with the "how big does it get"/"what will it look like" SVG diagrams, those are incredibly helpful. https://indigene.app/plants/symphyotrichum-subspicatum https://indigene.app/plants/juncus-patens Very helpful for choosing plants.

items.name: Flora Incognita
items.summary: A free, ad-free mobile app for identifying plants from photos.
items.why_included: It has a direct recommendation plus a successful first-hand identification report.
items.evidence: One commenter strongly recommended it for quick plant identification; another used it on a mystery houseplant.

evidence_sources.author: iammjm
evidence_sources.excerpt: I can strongly recommend the mobile app Flora Incognita for quickly identifying plants. It’s made by one of the German universities so it’s free, don’t have ads, and don’t collect your personal data. I even showed it to my mum and she loves it

evidence_sources.author: otherayden
evidence_sources.excerpt: Thank you for the rec, I used it to identify a mystery house plant I was gifted :)

items.name: Libdragon
items.source_story_title: How to Make a Nintendo 64 Game in 2026
items.summary: An open-source SDK for making games for the Nintendo 64.
items.why_included: The concrete praise cites rapid recent progress and unusually capable demos.
items.evidence: A commenter praised the core team and pointed to advanced demos as a reason to follow the project.

evidence_sources.author: Mizza
evidence_sources.excerpt: Libdragon has been improved massively in the past year or so, there are now simple demo games that show capabilities far beyond the original N64 games (bump mapping textures, HDR, seamless loading of massive overworld maps, etc.) Really talented core team, fun to give them a follow. Demos: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XP8g2ngHftY

items.name: PS1 Bare Metal
items.source_story_title: How to Make a Nintendo 64 Game in 2026
items.summary: A minimalist tutorial series for PlayStation 1 homebrew development.
items.why_included: It was explicitly recommended as modern learning material over old SDK-era examples.
items.evidence: Its author encouraged prospective PS1 homebrew developers to use modern tooling and linked the tutorial series.

evidence_sources.author: spicyjpeg
evidence_sources.excerpt: I am still amazed my own minimalist PS1 tutorial series [1] became as popular as it did, given that prior to it basically all learning material on the internet was written around the decent-for-the-time-but-horrible-now Sony SDK and often based on 30-year-old example code full of 30-year-old C practices (in particular the complete disregard for aliasing and concurrency, which resulted in plenty of headaches once people started using those ancient libraries and example code with modern GCC). We even have bleeding-edge C++ SDK options [2] complete with an STL and coroutine support, so if anybody here wants to try their hand at PS1 homebrew development I would highly encourage checking out the

items.name: Eve
items.source_story_title: Show HN: The Channels SDK – Bring Any Agent to Any Channel (Slack, MS Teams)
items.summary: A self-hostable agent runtime with TUI, GitHub, and chat-channel support.
items.why_included: A first-hand user called it well thought out, including its sandbox and scheduling abstractions.
items.evidence: A commenter reported that Eve works well across TUI, GitHub, and non-chat channels while remaining self-hostable.

evidence_sources.author: mrud
evidence_sources.excerpt: I have been using eve - https://eve.dev/ recently and it was just really nice and well thought out. It also supports TUI, github and other non chat channels. The integration and abstraction with sandboxes, cron etc. is very nicely done but you still can self host it.

items.name: ChatJimmy
items.source_story_title: AMD acquires Taalas to boost inference performance by etching models in silicon
items.summary: A public demo of extremely high-throughput language-model inference.
items.why_included: Multiple commenters singled out the experience as unusually compelling despite the small model.
items.evidence: Two commenters described the demo as magical and unusually impressive relative to typical model updates.

evidence_sources.author: wxw
evidence_sources.excerpt: I freakin' love this demo. It feels magical.

evidence_sources.author: appplication
evidence_sources.excerpt: This is the coolest LLM thing I’ve seen since the original ChatGPT announcement a few years ago. IMO much more impressive than marginal gains of frontier models.

items.name: Arcane Dimensions
items.summary: A large single-player Quake mod with new maps, mechanics, and enemies.
items.why_included: It received an unusually emphatic direct recommendation from a Quake player.
items.evidence: A commenter called it the best single-player FPS experience, praising its maps, mechanics, and enemies.

evidence_sources.author: namdnay
evidence_sources.excerpt: If you read this and you haven’t played arcane dimensions yet, drop everything and go and do that. It makes the quake the best single player FPS ever. The mechanics are even better than vanilla quake, the maps are gorgeous, the enemies diverse and fun. Absolute perfection

items.name: Scientific Babel
items.summary: A history of how English became the dominant language of science.
items.why_included: The recommendation is specific and fits readers interested in language and scientific history.
items.evidence: A commenter recommended Michael D. Gordin’s book for its account of languages used in science over time.

evidence_sources.author: rhodin
evidence_sources.excerpt: I'd also recommend "Scientific Babel How Science Was Done Before and After Global English" by Michael D. Gordin [0]. It goes into detail about which languages scientists have used over time. [0] https://press.uchicago.edu/ucp/books/book/chicago/S/bo145049...

items.name: Woodpecker CI
items.source_story_title: GitHub Actions and Pages are experiencing degraded availability
items.why_included: It was offered as a practical, explicitly capable alternative during a GitHub Actions outage.
items.evidence: A commenter recommended self-hosting Woodpecker, describing it as easy to use and capable.

evidence_sources.author: timetraveller26
evidence_sources.excerpt: If anybody is looking for alternatives, self host Woodpecker is really easy and it's a very capable CI/CD https://woodpecker-ci.org/docs/intro

items.name: Transitous
items.source_story_title: My phone detects going on a run as “someone snatching my phone and running off”
items.summary: An open-source public-transit routing engine with configurable first- and last-mile choices.
items.why_included: It offers controls that directly address the discussion’s complaint about routing defaults.
items.evidence: A commenter recommended Transitous for configurable walking, transit, and micromobility options.

evidence_sources.author: urineaut
evidence_sources.excerpt: Depending on where you live there is Transitous: https://transitous.org/ It's a FOSS public transport routing engine. In the options you can select what type and how much time you want to spend on the first and last "mile" (even something like bike/scooter sharing). It uses open data or data connectors for the routing. And being FOSS, if there is no data connector yet for you region, it may be interesting to contribute one if there is a sane way to query the data from the local transport compan(y|ies).

items.name: Ironwail
items.summary: A modern source port for playing Quake and its community expansions.
items.why_included: The recommendation gives a specific, practical reason to choose it with the current remaster.
items.evidence: A commenter recommended Ironwail for the Quake remaster’s PAK files and Steam achievements.

evidence_sources.author: Lammy
evidence_sources.excerpt: PROTIP: Install the Kex-engine remaster, but then actually play IronWail: https://github.com/andrei-drexler/ironwail It's a real IdTech source port that will load the Remaster's PAKs and pretend to be the Remaster to Steam for achievement unlocks. Dimension of the Machine was fantastic so I'm hyped to play Dawn of the Machine tonight :D
